text:
mira: Heads-up — we got a customer report where streaming reconnects are producing duplicate chunks and failing our checkpointing. Happens when client reconnects and hits a different backend pool (dedicated -> hosted). Noticed after a canary change to routing policy. :frowning:
alex: ugh. do we have logs/ids? is it WS or SSE? sounds like resume token / seq mismatch.
mira: WebSocket + resume token. snippet from client logs:
```
resume_token=eyJr... seq=1 expected=3456
server: accepted resume but sent history starting 1
```
jon: hmm if they land on a different instance the KV cache for the token may not exist. our resume is per-process not global. that would explain dupes + wrong seq.
sam: are we routing by connection id or by customer? the recent change made routing cheaper by not sticking to pool if idle for >20s.
kelly: that was the canary: change to dynamic routing to reduce wasted slots. but we intended to keep sticky routing for active streams — looks like the threshold was too low.
alex: quick thought: add a small grace window where we reroute reconnects to the same pool if resume_token present. fallback to full resync if not found.
mira: agree. but we need to be careful about capacity — that defeats some of the new policy. maybe use a probabilistic sticky policy for enterprise customers?
jon: also need telemetry: emit metric when resume_token accepted but seq mismatch. tag by route_variant, pool_id, customer_tier so we can see how often this happens and which policy triggers it.
dev-bot: deploy #canary/streaming-routing v2026.03.10 started by ci
sam: operationally, is it safe to treat a resume token miss as idempotent restart on client side? some clients are stateful and will reapply prompts.
mira: client-side should tolerate restarts but many integrate with local dedupe. still, better server-side guarantees.
kelly: UX concern: Console rollout page should show "streaming sticky policy" state per customer when toggling. PMs want to be able to preview which customers will be affected by policy changes before rollout.
alex: implementation plan: 1) quick metric + alert, 2) short-term sticky-on-resume for 60s, 3) longer-term: shared resume store (redis) or token sharding by hash so any pool can validate resume. prefer sharded token hashing.
jon: +1 on sharded hashing. if we key by resume_token -> pool_id via consistent hash, we get cheap routing without global store.
sam: I'll add a flag to policy service to prefer consistent-hash routing when resume header present. we can roll that in canary.
mira: can someone own a small postmortem if this affects >1 customer? tag me. we should also add a test harness that simulates reconnects across pools.
ops-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-58 — streaming-resume-mismatch (severity: medium)
kelly: I can update the rollout checklist to include a "streaming resume smoke test" and console flag for preview lists.
alex: PR incoming with metrics + sticky-on-resume patch. will request review after tests.
mira: thanks — please add unit/integration test for WS resume where server restarts, and include flakiness monitor in the console dashboard (new chart: resume success rate by pool).
jon: also export a trace span for resume validation latency so we can see cross-pool penalties.
sam: noted. scheduling a quick sync later today to align on rollout cadence. :calendar:
mira: perfect. tagging for follow-ups: @alex @jon @sam @kelly. will triage after PR lands.
